summary: No Medium-or-above candidate. The fixed-point and delivery semantics of R5 were checked across send_cmio_response (C++ template, native API, JSON-RPC and Lua bindings, regenerated SendCmioResponse.sol, Dave's CartesiStateTransition and DaveConsensus.provideMerkleRootOfInput), interpret() and get_state_break_reason precedence, uarch_step/uarch_interpret (C++ and regenerated UArchStep.sol), uarch_reset_state (C++ and UArchReset.sol), collect_mcycle_root_hashes, collect_mcycle_bundle, collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes, collect_uarch_cycle_bundle, and the PRT referee model and honest player in doc/recipes/prt.lua. They were all found consistent. A differential experiment was run on baremetal-template: rejection exactly at imcyclemax, one mcycle after it and one mcycle before it. Native run, a uarch step-by-step replay with C++ log/verify of every step and reset, collect_mcycle_root_hashes and collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes all agreed. A rejection on the instruction that reaches imcyclemax is reported as yielded_manually and is reverted to the pre-delivery hash everywhere. A stop at imcyclemax one cycle earlier is reported as mcycle_overflow and is not reverted. The one candidate below is a Low-rated guest-software observation.

candidates.title: libcmt cmt_gio_request accepts any 16-bit domain, including RX_ACCEPTED/RX_REJECTED, producing a manual yield the emulator treats as finishing an input
candidates.location: sys-utils/libcmt/src/rollup.c cmt_gio_request (builds struct cmt_io_yield {.dev=HTIF_DEVICE_YIELD,.cmd=HTIF_YIELD_CMD_MANUAL,.reason=req->domain,...}); emulator side: src/send-cmio-response.cpp isYieldedManualWith(tohost, RX_ACCEPTED), src/uarch-reset-state.cpp (revert on RX_REJECTED)
candidates.description: cmt_gio_request puts the caller-supplied domain into the manual-yield reason field without range checking. A GIO request with domain 1 (RX_ACCEPTED) is indistinguishable from cmt_rollup_finish(accept): the next advance-state delivery is applied as the GIO response, and the tx buffer (holding the GIO id, not an outputs Merkle root) becomes what A5 extracts as the outputs root. A GIO request with domain 2 (RX_REJECTED) makes the protocol revert to the pre-delivery state. The emulator is behaving as specified (section 4: 'the transition function interprets only ... the accepted and rejected reasons of a manual yield'). Any defect is in the guest library's API contract.
candidates.trigger: The application author calls cmt_gio_request with domain 1 or 2, or an input steers an application that forwards an input-chosen domain to cmt_gio_request.
candidates.reachability: Reachable only if an application passes such a domain. GIO domains are meant for host-side generic I/O (the rollup-http tests use 0x100). In a PRT deployment, any GIO manual yield other than accepted/rejected is a stall anyway.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: arguably, 'An application that is not correctly designed, other than through a defect in guest software that section 3 puts in scope.' Using GIO with a reserved domain is outside the rollup interface. 2 Role: Guest software (AUDIT.md table: machine-guest-tools). Section 3: 'A defect in them is in scope only where an application depends on them as documented, and would be correctly designed if they worked as documented ... Any other defect in them is Low.' 3 High/Medium: none applies. 4 Critical: needs an application that would be correctly designed and that an input can push into deviating from the rollup interface (R7 yield interface). No documented use of GIO with domains 1 or 2 was found, so this is not shown. 5 Low: 'a defect in guest software that only an application outside its intended use can reach'.
candidates.threat_to_goal: None for a correctly designed application. At most an API foot-gun that lets a misused GIO call settle the GIO id as an outputs root, or silently revert.
candidates.evidence: Code reading of the v0.18.1-test1 source (git clone at the tag): accepted()/revert() and cmt_gio_request in rollup.c. No dynamic test.
candidates.test_idea: A bare-metal or libcmt guest calls cmt_gio_request(domain=1) and then a delivery is made. The test asserts that libcmt returned -EINVAL for a reserved domain, so the yield never happens and the machine is not at an rx-accepted manual yield.

not_covered: The EVM (Solidity) side of the fixed-point experiments: the step-EVM anvil was not started. Agreement of UArchStep/UArchReset/SendCmioResponse.sol with C++ was checked only by reading the generated code, which is identical in control flow and read order.

The Dave tournament contracts beyond CartesiStateTransition, the input witness and the A5 machine validity proof: matches, timeouts, propagation of uarch results, and how the last leaf is authenticated (A1/A2).

The cartesi-machine.lua CLI computation-hash builders beyond a skim. Its --print-uarch-cycle-root-hashes passes a fake {revert,revert} revert tail, but cmio mode is excluded, so only a guest that rejects without any delivery reaches it (diagnostic only, not reported).
The PRT player restart path, stored-machine cache and bridge (prt-bridge.lua, crisium.lua), including fixed-point handling after a restart.

Worst-case uarch cycles per mcycle (whether some instruction can need >= 2^20-1 uarch cycles, which makes the native collector throw 'uarch reached its maximum cycle'). This belongs to R4/R12, not measured.
Inspect-state deliveries (outside verified history), and soft-yield and console break interactions with fixed points under the native API.
Linux cmio kernel driver (out of scope) and the rollup-http server's handling of yield reasons.
The interaction of fixed points with RTC/timer interrupts across uarch vs native (an R2 angle).
